nodes.summary: The logistic equation: `x'(t) = s x(t) (1 - x(t))`.
nodes.title: Sweep trajectory solves the logistic equation

nodes.summary: In the star-genealogy model the one-sided integrated haplotype homozygosity is `1 / (2 r T)`.
nodes.title: One-sided iHH in the star-genealogy model

nodes.summary: In the star-genealogy model the two-sided integrated haplotype homozygosity is `1 / (r T)`.
nodes.title: Two-sided iHH in the star-genealogy model

nodes.summary: The two-sided integrated haplotype homozygosity of Voight et al.: the sum of the one-sided integrals in the two chromosome directions.
nodes.title: Two-sided integrated haplotype homozygosity

nodes.summary: The one-sided integrated haplotype homozygosity: the area under the EHH decay curve in one direction from the focal site. Voight et al.'s iHH integrates in both directions; see `ihh_twoSided`.
nodes.title: One-sided integrated haplotype homozygosity

nodes.summary: In the star-genealogy model the integrated haplotype score is the log ratio of the two ages, so the recombination rate cancels.
nodes.title: iHS as the log ratio of genealogy ages

nodes.summary: The integrated haplotype score is negative exactly when the derived allele's star genealogy is the younger one, i.e. when the derived allele swept faster.
nodes.title: iHS is negative exactly when the derived allele is younger

nodes.summary: The integrated haplotype score of Voight et al. (2006): the log ratio of the integrated haplotype homozygosities of the ancestral and the derived allele, whose star genealogies have ages `T_A` and `T_D`. The factor of two between the one-sided and two-sided integrals cancels in this ratio.
nodes.title: Integrated haplotype score (iHS)

nodes.summary: A complete sweep in a population of `N` diploids, from a single copy `1 / (2N)` to `1 - 1 / (2N)`, takes exactly `(2 / s) log (2N - 1)` generations in the deterministic logistic model. (The familiar `(2 / s) log (2Ns)` is the conditional expected duration of the corresponding stochastic sweep, a different quantity.)
nodes.title: Duration of a complete deterministic sweep

nodes.summary: The time to reach a higher frequency is positive.
nodes.title: Positivity of the sweep duration

nodes.summary: The time the logistic trajectory with selection coefficient `s` takes to go from frequency `a` to frequency `b`: `(1/s) log (b (1 - a) / (a (1 - b)))`, the difference of the logits divided by `s`.
nodes.title: Duration of a logistic sweep between two frequencies

nodes.summary: Haplotype homozygosity decays with the window length.
nodes.title: Star-genealogy EHH decays with window length

nodes.summary: The star-genealogy EHH is the square of the probability that a Poisson number of recombination events with mean `r d T` on one lineage is zero.
nodes.title: Star-genealogy EHH as a squared Poisson zero probability

nodes.summary: Combining the exact sweep duration with the star-genealogy decay: after a complete sweep of a favourable allele with selection coefficient `s` in a population of `N` diploids, the extended haplotype homozygosity at genetic distance `d` is the power law `(2N - 1) ^ (-(4 r d / s))`.
nodes.title: Power-law EHH after a complete sweep

nodes.summary: The probability that two carriers of a swept allele are identical over a window of genetic length `d`, in the star-genealogy model of Voight et al. (2006): all carriers coalesce at the start of the sweep, a time `T` ago, and the pair is identical exactly when neither of its two lineages recombined, each at rate `r * d` per unit time.
nodes.title: EHH in the star-genealogy sweep model

nodes.summary: The trajectory stays strictly between `0` and `1`.
nodes.title: Sweep trajectory stays strictly between 0 and 1

nodes.summary: `sweepDuration s a b` is the exact time at which the trajectory started at `a` reaches `b`.
nodes.title: Sweep trajectory reaches its target at the sweep duration

nodes.summary: The logistic trajectory of a favourable allele with genic selection coefficient `s`, starting from frequency `x₀`: the solution of `x' = s x (1 - x)` with `x 0 = x₀` (Maynard Smith and Haigh 1974).
nodes.title: Logistic trajectory of a selective sweep

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
